generic: "Whole town fits on a postcard. We remember who left and who came back."
"That house by the water has its lights on again. Nobody's seen who lives there in years."
"Watch the tall grass past the fence. Small things in there, big opinions."
"Sea-salt morning. The tide goes out, the kids go north, and the town counts who returns."
"Every champion the radio ever named came from a town this size. The road north remembers them all."
rivalAhead: "Your rival's been pacing the town gate since sunrise, rehearsing a speech. Act surprised."
"Two starters walked out of that lab today. This town has watched that story open a hundred ways — it never agrees on the ending."

generic: "Dust gets into everything here. Your boots, your lungs, your win record."
"Free to watch the dojo. Costs plenty to step on the mat."
"The house at the quarry's edge stays unlocked. Nobody locks it. Nobody goes in."
"Quarry pays by the ton, the gym pays in bruises. Both crews drink at the same bar."
preGym: "The Leader tests your stamina, not your luck. The quarry crews bet on challengers — right now the odds aren't kind to you."
"Gym lights stay on until somebody knocks them out. The whole shift watches when somebody tries."
postGym: "Word beat you to the bar: the Leader lost. Half the quarry owes the other half money."
"One badge in, and the Leader's been telling everyone you earned it. That's rarer than the badge."

generic: "Every barista in this town can recite a movepool. It's a little much."
"They say the Dojo Master boxed a Machamp once. Don't test it."
"Kid down the lane keeps a list of every trainer who comes through. Swears she's seen your name before."
"The Tutor talks fast and won't repeat for free. Bring a notebook, or a good memory."
"Granny at the stone stall reads evolutions in the rock grain. She's wrong less often than the textbooks."
preGym: "The café crowd already handicapped your gym match. Buy a coffee and they'll show you the whiteboard."
"This Leader studies a challenger's moveset before every bout. Assume yours is on the board already."
postGym: "The cafés will argue your gym match for a week. The move you closed with is on the specials board."
"Two badges deep and the Tutor's asking about you. That's the local version of famous."

generic: "Half these textbooks are wrong by next year. The Gym Leader isn't."
"There's a library shelf nobody reshelves. Take what you find, leave what finds you."
"Lectures run late. So do the rematches out back."
"Freshmen post your losses, seniors post your wins. Pick your rivals early."
preGym: "The Leader grades on tempo, coverage, and nerve. Nobody's ever gotten full marks."
"Exam season for them, gym season for you. Same hallway, same dread, better prizes."
postGym: "Your gym match made the syllabus. 'Case study,' they're calling it."
"Three badges reads like a thesis half-defended. The back half is where committees get mean."
rivalAhead: "Someone matching your rival's description was drilling switch-ins on the quad all morning. That's for you."
"Your rival checked the standings board twice today. Whatever they saw, they left grinning."

generic: "Twelve floors of want, and a rooftop you can see four routes from. Mind your wallet on three of them."
"The Department Store hires half the town and sells to the other half."
"The elevator's been 'temporarily out' for six years. The stairwell knows everyone's business."
"Floor staff quote prices from memory. The loading-dock alley quotes better ones. Skip the alley."
preGym: "The Leader works a register upstairs some mornings. Sizes up challengers by what they buy."
"Four badges is where the league starts keeping notes. This gym is where the notebooks come out."
postGym: "They're looping your badge match on the demo screens. Aisle five, between the fridges."
"Halfway to eight. The store's already selling a 'challenger special' with your silhouette on it."

generic: "Ranger boots, hunter boots, poacher boots. Every kind of mud meets at this gate."
"Don't name what you might have to release. Costs you more that way."
"Half the badges in this town were won at the slots. Don't ask which half."
"Fountain shuts off at midnight. Some nights it runs anyway. Maintenance, they say."
"The Safari takes your money and your patience. The casino skips the patience part."
preGym: "Last easy night before the climb. The Leader likes a crowd, and the rooftop bar likes a rematch."
"Slots pay out in coins, the gym pays out in respect. Locals will tell you which one's rigged."
postGym: "Five badges. The pit boss comped your drink and the rangers waved you through. Fame here is quiet like that."
"Badge like that, the casino floor gets friendlier and the odds get worse. Not a coincidence."

generic: "This city eats trainers and prints champions. Take notes."
"The square's big screen loops the same champion's walk-on. Same face, long as anyone bothers to remember."
"Nobody's from here. Everybody's becoming someone here."
"The skyline ate the route signs years ago. Ask directions and you'll get three rival opinions."
preGym: "Six gyms in, the crowds stop being kind. This Leader sells out the arena on a weeknight."
"The gym runs a waiting list. Somebody gave up their slot this morning. It's yours now."
postGym: "Six badges. The big screen looped your finisher twice before lunch. Enjoy it — this city forgets by Friday."
"The arena crowd knows your name now. Half of them bet against you. They'll deny it."
rivalAhead: "Your rival gave an interview at the arena gate. Kept pointing at the road out of town."
"Someone left a note at the gym desk: 'Tell them I went ahead.' The clerk figures you'd know the handwriting."

generic: "Thin air at the pass keeps the tourists down in the lowlands."
"Veterans drink here between rematches. Buy a round, get a story."
"Every story at this altitude is a warning wearing a smile."
"Somebody walks the pass at night who shouldn't be able to. Wears a cap like yours. The veterans stopped pointing it out."
preGym: "Seven badges deep, nobody carries you up the mountain. The Leader here has ended more runs than the weather."
"Colress cleared his roof-lab schedule when he heard a challenger was in town. He hates waiting. Move quick."
postGym: "Seven badges. The veterans stopped telling you stories and started asking for yours."
"One badge left. The wind carries bell-sound down from the last town. Some say it rings early for the worthy."

generic: "Last gym before the Plateau. People travel weeks just to lose here."
"The bells ring for every challenger. They don't ring twice."
"Bells, pilgrims, one last gate. Past it the cities run out."
"Take the long look back. Six routes made you. The seventh won't be a route."
preGym: "The bell-keeper polishes the challenger bell every morning. He's been polishing slower since you arrived."
"They built the eighth gym like a cathedral for a reason. People leave changed, or they don't leave champions."
postGym: "The eighth badge. The bells rang for you at dawn — the keeper says they sounded different. He won't say how."
"A masked figure was asking after you. Wouldn't leave a name. Left the innkeeper's hands shaking, though."

generic: "This is the room. No badges past that door, only legacies."
"Cameras are rolling. Smile or don't. It's your face."
"Different currency past this door. Legacies, not badges."
"The portrait wall has one empty frame at the end. Clean glass. Nobody ever books it."
"Bring everything. The Plateau keeps whatever you can't carry."
"You walked out of the Hall and the corridor lights flickered. Nobody here will say who's waiting past it."
"Your name's on the wall, and something is still standing between you and the door home."
"The staff won't look down the far corridor. Whatever asked after you hasn't left."
"Trainers still gather here, even after the credits rolled."
"Your name's on the Hall. Go look. Some mornings folks swear the date beside it reads wrong."
"Credits rolled and nobody left. Tells you something about the worthy."
"The Crucible crowd doesn't care about your title. That's the appeal."
